title: Practice 7: в- and вы-: in, and out

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.why: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress). — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.context: The verb **написать** is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress).

exercises.why: **вы́вести** — **выводи́ть** — to take out, to lead out, to bring out, to move out; to help out (help someone to get off); to withdraw, to call off (troops). **вы́везти** — **вывози́ть** — to take out (by vehicle), to remove; to deliver. **вы́лезть** — **вылеза́ть** — to get out, to climb out, to get off; (of hair) to fall out, to come out. — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_grammar#Verbs_of_motion, CC BY-SA 4.0)  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: вы́вести** — **выводи́ть — to take out, to lead out, to bring out, to move out; to help out (help someone to get off); to withdraw, to call off (troops).

exercises.why: **вле́зть** — **влеза́ть** — to get into (something, also figurative), to climb into, to scramble into; to fit in, to go in. **вы́йти** — **выходи́ть** — to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published. **вы́ехать** — **выезжа́ть** — to exit, to go out (by vehicle). **вы́лететь** — **вылета́ть** — to fly out, to fly (from a place); (computing) to crash. **вы́бежать** — **выбега́ть** — to run out (outside). **вы́нести** — **выноси́ть** — to carry out, to take out, to bring out, to remove; to transfer. — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_grammar#Verbs_of_motion, CC BY-SA 4.0)  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: The verbs въезжать (to drive in) and выезжать (to drive out) belong to the 1st ("-е-") type of conjugation (like читать): я въезжаю, ты въезжаешь … они въезжают. *Я вхожу в эту комнату каждый день. Я входил в эту комнату каждый день. Я буду входить в эту комнату каждый день. Я вошёл в комнату и открыл окно. Я войду в комнату и открою окно.* — DLI, Lesson 33.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: After slapping Tom, Mary ran out of the room.
exercises.why: The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят. The verbs въезжать (to drive in) and выезжать (to drive out) belong to the 1st ("-е-") type of conjugation (like читать): я въезжаю, ты въезжаешь … они въезжают. Ввозить — ввезти — to haul in, to import; вывозить — вывезти — to haul out, to export. Note the special use of the verbs "ввозить" and "вывозить": Англия ввозит зерно, а вывозит машины. — England imports grain and exports machinery. Note also the nouns: ввоз — import; вывоз —… — DLI, Lesson 33.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.ru: Залепив Тому пощёчину, Маша ___ из комнаты.
exercises.context: The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. (DLI, Lesson 33)
